request_raw: Update the orders database schema to add a 'customer_notes' column and a 'delivery_instructions' field for order fulfillment, ensuring existing orders and running queries remain compatible.
request_normalized: Apply database schema migration adding order delivery fields while maintaining non-breaking backward compatibility with existing stored records.
intended_behavior: Orders table adds optional customer_notes (text, nullable) and delivery_instructions (text, nullable)
Existing database rows created prior to the migration deserialize and query cleanly without null constraint crashes
New checkout requests can supply or omit delivery fields without validation errors
Database downgrade / rollback script restores the previous schema state without catastrophic data loss

functional_requirements.description: Order model includes customer_notes: str | None with nullable=True
Order model includes delivery_instructions: str | None with nullable=True
CheckoutRequest accepts optional customer_notes and delivery_instructions
CheckoutResponse includes delivery fields if provided

invariants.description: The migration must preserve required application and data compatibility. Migrations must not add non-nullable columns without defaults to tables with existing records.
Queries selecting existing orders must not fail after schema migration is applied.
Database rollback must cleanly revert the schema without locking or corrupting order tables.

api_implications: POST /checkout request schema gains optional customer_notes: str | null
POST /checkout request schema gains optional delivery_instructions: str | null
data_schema_implications: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN customer_notes TEXT NULL
ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN delivery_instructions TEXT NULL
security_concerns: Customer notes must be sanitized against cross-site scripting (XSS) when rendered in admin dashboards
SQL DDL statements must be executed through parameterized migration engine (no raw string formatting)
rollback_requirements: Run migration downgrade to drop new columns
Remove new fields from SQLAlchemy Order model
notes: S05 secondary benchmark scenario: Schema Migration Compatibility. Seeded defect: Migration defines new column as nullable=False with no default value on an existing table with records, causing SQLite/PostgreSQL operational errors on existing rows and breaking older application instances. Expected adversarial concern: Bob identifies schema migration incompatibility with existing data (inv-01). Expected verification behavior: FAILED on test_migration_preserves_existing_order_record_compatibility; VERIFIED when column is marked nullable=True with safe defaults.
